Bloomberg reports that Apple's smart home product plans include devices, cameras, and cameras in collaboration with LG. Here are the details.

Apple partners with LG to launch home connected devices

According to Bloomberg, Apple and LG have been collaborating to develop a range of home connected products as part of an upcoming smart home hub accessory, marking a "formal reboot of HomeKit."

Bloomberg noted that the products include "doorbells, thermostats... smart locks, indoor security cameras, outdoor security cameras, and floodlight cameras."

Gurman mentioned that although Apple and LG are "collaborating on these accessories, the products will be released under the LG brand," adding that "the Korean company is responsible for manufacturing and product support" and has recently applied for regulatory approval.

It is worth noting that although these products are part of Apple's broader push into the connected home market and are expected to be unveiled next week alongside a brand-new smart home hub, an updated Apple TV, and a new HomePod mini, Bloomberg stated that "these products are not expected to hit the consumer market for at least a few more months."

Here is the Bloomberg report:

In recent weeks, LG has filed applications for regulatory approval for these devices, including submissions to the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) and product certification body UL Solutions. The databases of both organizations often contain application documents showing product names, specifications, features, and design drawings of accessories. These include products labeled as LG Video Doorbell Wired, LG Floodlight Cam, LG Outdoor Cam Plug-In, LG Indoor Cam Plug-In, LG Smart Deadbolt Lock, LG Smart Thermostat, and LG Temperature Sensor. LG has requested that product photos and further details be kept confidential until early next year. The application documents do not mention Apple's involvement.

The most liked comment was posted by Scott D.

Well, it's hard to get excited about LG products — after all, their company TVs record conversations in your living room and send them off to who knows where...

In terms of connectivity and standards, the report noted that many devices will support Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Thread, and Matter. The report also mentioned that the smart lock features UWB (Ultra-Wideband), enabling automatic unlocking and other short-range detection functions.

Finally, the report noted that for both Apple and LG, these products mark a broader expansion in the smart home market, with Apple hoping to inject new momentum into its home ecosystem:

It is worth emphasizing that although the timing of this report comes just after Apple announced it will launch the long-rumored "HomePad" smart home hub and other products next week, these LG-manufactured accessories are not expected to hit the consumer market for at least a few more months.
